questions.prompt: Why does the harness put TypeScript declarations of the tools into the system prompt?
options: So the model writes calls with the exact names, arguments and result types
So the provider can check the types
So the tools run without the pipeline
questions.explanation: The declarations come from the tool schemas, so the model knows each function's name, arguments and result before it writes the program.

questions.prompt: Why do the call messages use a separate pipe, not the program's normal output?
options: JSON cannot pass through normal output
So text the program prints never mixes with the call messages
So the model can read the messages
questions.explanation: A program may print anything. A separate pipe keeps every control line a clean JSON object that the harness can parse.

questions.prompt: The harness replies to id 2 with an error. What happens inside the program?
options: The promise for that call rejects with a ToolCallError, which the program can catch
The call returns an empty object
questions.explanation: An error reply rejects the waiting promise with a ToolCallError naming the tool, so the program can handle it and continue.
